one_liner: Header-only C++11 YAML 1.2 DOM parser/emitter that parses 7.3-7.7x faster than yaml-cpp in the project's benchmark.
what_it_does: Parses YAML 1.2 (block and flow styles, anchors/aliases, tags, multi-document streams, UTF-8/16/32 with BOM detection) from strings, iterators, FILE* or std::istream into an owning fkyaml::node tree, lets you edit it, and serializes it back to YAML. The API is its own value-type DOM: fkyaml::node::deserialize()/deserialize_docs(), operator[]/at(), as_seq()/as_map(), get_value<T>(), plus from_node/to_node hooks for your own types. It is not source-compatible with yaml-cpp's YAML::Load/YAML::Node.
how_it_is_fast: One up-front pass validates UTF-8 (transcoding UTF-16/32 or stripping CRs only when needed). For contiguous LF-only UTF-8 input, the lexer then runs directly on the caller's buffer and emits tokens as non-owning str_view slices, which avoids copying; the maintainer's PR #448 credits 'reducing redundant object creations and data copies'. Scalars are typed during parsing by a length-switched scanner and converted immediately, with hand-written bounds-checked integer parsing and std::from_chars for floats under C++17. As a result, nodes hold bool/int64_t/double natively, and only multi-line or escaped scalars use a scratch buffer (PR #409 split scalar parsing out of the lexer). The deserializer is an iterative state machine over an explicit std::deque context stack, not recursive descent. There is no SIMD; delimiter searches are per-byte char_traits::find loops.
when_to_use: Replacing yaml-cpp where YAML load time matters. The benchmark inputs were an 8.8 KB block-YAML file (ubuntu.yml), a 0.7 MB YAML file and a 1.7 MB JSON file, and fkYAML was about 7.5x faster than yaml-cpp on all three.

You want header-only, zero-dependency integration (a single-header node.hpp is provided, plus a CMake package and pkg-config) that builds as C++11 on old toolchains. CI covers GCC 5.3 to 16, Clang 3.4 to 21, AppleClang and VS 2022/2026.
Code reads many typed values after parsing: ints, floats, bools and nulls are converted once during deserialize, so get_value<int>() or as_bool() does not re-parse text.

Inputs arrive in mixed encodings (UTF-16/UTF-32 LE/BE with or without BOM), or JSON has to go through the same parser. In the benchmark, fkYAML's best absolute speed was on citm_catalog.json (121 MiB/s).
Parse, modify and re-serialize workflows where an editable DOM with value semantics is more convenient than an event API.
when_not_to_use: You need the fastest C++ YAML parser for typical block-style files. In the same harness, rapidyaml was ~2x faster on ubuntu.yml (151/132 vs 76 MiB/s); fkYAML led it by only 4-11% on the two citm files.

Large documents or memory-constrained targets. The library is DOM-only with no event/streaming API. FILE* and istream inputs are read fully into a std::string first. Every string, sequence and mapping is a separate std::allocator heap object, and each node also carries a shared_ptr and a unique_ptr. There is no allocator or arena hook, and memory use is not benchmarked.

Documents that depend on duplicate keys, source key order or YAML 1.1 semantics. Mappings default to std::map, so duplicate keys are rejected and output keys come out sorted. %YAML directives are ignored and the 1.2 rules apply. The source has no merge-key (<<) handling.

Untrusted input in security-sensitive services without your own fuzzing. In Aug 2026, fuzzing found out-of-bounds reads, release-mode SEGVs, a leak, and a stack overflow from self-referential aliases (#536, #546, #548). All were fixed for v0.4.4/v0.5.0, but that is recent hardening.
Code that needs API stability: the library is pre-1.0, and v0.5.0 (2026-09-17) removed APIs deprecated since v0.3.12 and v0.4.3 (node_t, type(), get_value_ref<T>(), and others).

integration.min_toolchain: C++11. CI tests GCC 5.3.1+, Clang 3.4.2+, AppleClang 15+, Visual Studio 17 2022+ and IntelLLVM 2026.1. The std::from_chars float path needs C++17 with __cpp_lib_to_chars.
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS and Windows are CI-tested. The code is portable C++ with no SIMD or other architecture-specific code.
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. The headers have no mutable global or static state. All nodes of one document, including copies, share one std::shared_ptr to the document metainfo and anchor table.

gotchas: A string-key lookup (node["k"] or at("k")) first builds a temporary basic_node, which heap-allocates a std::string, then does an O(log n) std::map search. Non-const operator[] inserts a node on a miss. The insertion-order option, fkyaml::ordered_map, is a std::vector with linear-search find().

Every access through an anchor or alias node calls resolve_reference(). Since the fix for #548, that call walks the whole anchored subtree to detect self-references, so repeated access to large anchored subtrees costs O(subtree) each time.
CRLF input forces a full copy of the buffer (the docs say this); only contiguous LF-only UTF-8 is parsed in place. Serialization always writes LF.
Without C++17 <charconv> float support, each float scalar goes through std::stod on a temporary std::string, so the benchmark numbers may not hold for C++11/14 builds.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick fkYAML over rapidyaml when you want a header-only C++11 value-type DOM with scalars already typed and your inputs look like the large, JSON-like citm files, where it matched or slightly beat ryml; for small block YAML, ryml was ~2x faster. fkYAML beat libfyaml 2.1-2.6x in the same harness, but PipeYAML's yaml-cpp ratios come from a different harness, so the published data cannot rank the two.
verified_claims_summary: The project's Google Benchmark v1.9.5 harness deserializes an in-memory std::string of ubuntu.yml (8,819 B), citm_catalog.yml (717,429 B) and citm_catalog.json (1,727,204 B) into a DOM and destroys it each iteration. Single Release runs built with g++ 11.4.0 (fkYAML at -O2; yaml-cpp 0.9.0 under its own Release flags) on a Ryzen 7 5800H under WSL2 gave fkYAML 76.1/56.1/121.0 MiB/s against yaml-cpp's 10.1/7.3/16.7 MiB/s (7.5x/7.7x/7.3x); no third party has reproduced this, and yaml-cpp ran only 6 iterations on each citm file.
status_note: Actively maintained (v0.5.0 on 2026-09-17, commits through 2026-09-21, one open issue) and MIT-licensed, header-only and easy to vendor, but still pre-1.0 with recent API removals and a fresh round of fuzz-driven fixes.
